operations.name: David Watson

expected.charges: Aiding the 1858 Oberlin–Wellington Rescue of John Price, a fugitive from slavery, in violation of the Fugitive Slave Act of 1850.
expected.sentence:
Held April 15 – July 6, 1859 (about 82 days); no conviction.

Verdict as recorded: No — indictment dismissed July 6, 1859.

operations.source: https://www2.oberlin.edu/external/EOG/Oberlin-Wellington_Rescue/ClevelandHerald/The%20Cleveland%20Daily%20Herald%2004-15-1859%20The%20Thirtyseven%20in%20the%20Hands%20of%20the%20Marshal.htm — Cleveland Daily Herald, April 15, 1859, identifies David Watson among those in court and names the judge and district attorney. Names retained as printed, without unverified expansion. April 15 surrender/commitment is not substituted for an independently unresolved earlier arrest.

operations.name: Frank Cox

expected.name: Frank Cox
expected.description: Frank Cox was an IWW member from Eureka. Frank Cox received a four-year prison sentence for attending an IWW meeting and "taking minutes" and served in San Quentin from April 10, 1923, until his term expired.
expected.body:
1920s custody review: People v. Cox, 66 Cal.App.287,226 P.14 (March21,1924), identifies this as a California criminal-syndicalism prosecution, not a federal Espionage Act case. In the quoted trial exchange Cox explicitly identifies December26,1922 as the arrest date at Normana Hall; the sheriff confirms that Cox and McGrath were arrested together. That explicit answer supports the recorded arrest date, rather than merely using the offense date in the information. Other passages contain uncertain January references and an inconsistent letter date, so the precise original jail record remains worth checking. The existing April10,1923 San Quentin admission and year-only1925 release are retained, not newly verified by this decision.

Source: People v. Cox, California Court of Appeal, March21,1924. The appellate decision is not a physical release date.

operations.source: https://www.marxists.org/history/usa/pubs/dailyworker/1925/1925-ny/v02b-n297-NYE-dec-29-1925-DW-LOC.pdf — Daily Worker December 29, 1925 prisoner roster identifies Frank Cox at San Quentin, number 37701. Historical state prison number, not a BOP number. The roster also conflicts with the populated year-only 1925 release; existing endpoint preserved and flagged.

operations.name: William Wheeler

expected.charges: Organizing and leading the 1845 Port Tobacco mass escape from slavery.
expected.sentence:
Imprisoned at the Port Tobacco jail; he escaped and was never recaptured.

Verdict as recorded: Yes — tried in 1845; a special Maryland law was passed to ensure his life imprisonment.

updates.judge: Clement Dorsey and Alexander C. Magruder

operations.source: https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc5400/sc5496/015100/015156/html/015156bio.html — Maryland State Archives cites contemporary Charles County Court reporting. It explicitly dates death sentencing November 1, 1845 and names both presiding judges and prosecutor. Later law authorizes imprisonment in the event of commutation; it is not proof of actual release or commutation. Populated fields unchanged.

operations.name: Thomas Coleman Hawkins

expected.charges: Mutiny and riot (1917 Houston Riot courts-martial at Fort Sam Houston; convictions set aside 2023)
expected.prosecutor: Col. John A. Hull (Trial Judge Advocate)
expected.sentence:
Death by hanging (Dec 11, 1917)

Verdict as recorded: Yes — court-martial; conviction set aside Nov 2023

operations.source: https://justiceforthe24th.org/soldier/pfc-thomas-c-hawkins/ — individual military-history account identifies Hawkins, his December 11, 1917 execution, and final letter. Death in custody endpoint, not release. Existing prisoner death date and all other fields preserved.

operations.name: Ciaron O'Reilly

expected.sentence: Held about two months after the action, then released pre-trial on bail on March 6, 1991

updates.charges: Conspiracy and destruction of United States government property — January 1, 1991 ANZUS Ploughshares action at Griffiss Air Force Base.

operations.source: https://www.greenleft.org.au/1993/119/world/when-ploughshares-met-us-air-force — October 20, 1993 interview with O’Reilly expressly distinguishes the two indicted charges from sabotage, which was not charged. Fill missing charges on pretrial-detention case only, matching the same action already represented by the sentencing case; do not merge or extend separate custody intervals.

expected.name: Kit Havice
expected.description: Kit Havice participated in the integrated CNVA peace walk and was jailed in Albany, Georgia, in December 1963.

updates.body:
Photo credit

The Champion Newspaper, Kathy Mitchell’s February 11, 2019 interview with Kit Havice. Photographer not specified. Exact rectangular crop (300, 205, 790, 740) from the original 1080 by 1080 promotional image, retaining original pixels and removing surrounding headline and social-media graphics. Copyright retained by the source; no open license or permission claimed. Used for educational biographical identification at the site owner’s direction. Source interview and photograph.
